name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q01 - Common names and natural sources of carbonyl compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Compound)List-II (Natural Source)
A. VanillinI. Meadow sweet
B. SalicylaldehydeII. Vanilla beans
C. CinnamaldehydeIII. Red ants
D. Formic acidIV. Cinnamon

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the natural origin of Vanillin
Vanillin is a well-known aromatic aldehyde possessing a pleasant vanilla scent. In nature, it is extracted from vanilla beans. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the natural origin of Salicylaldehyde
Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) is naturally occurring and was historically isolated from the meadow sweet plant (Spiraea ulmaria). Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the natural origin of Cinnamaldehyde
Cinnamaldehyde (3-phenylprop-2-enal) is the organic compound that imparts distinctive aroma and flavour to the bark of cinnamon trees. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the natural origin of Formic acid
Formic acid (\(\mathrm{HCOOH}\)), the simplest carboxylic acid, was originally obtained by the destructive distillation of red ants (derived from the Latin word formica meaning ant). Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q02 - Common and IUPAC nomenclature of carbonyl compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Common Name)List-II (IUPAC Name)
A. AcroleinI. Pentanal
B. ValeraldehydeII. Prop-2-enal
C. PhthaldehydeIII. 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one
D. Mesityl oxideIV. Benzene-1,2-dicarbaldehyde

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the systematic nomenclature of Acrolein
Acrolein has the chemical formula \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH\text{-}CHO}\). The principal functional group is an aldehyde located at carbon-1, with an alkene unsaturation at carbon-2 of a three-carbon chain. Therefore, its IUPAC name is Prop-2-enal. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the systematic nomenclature of Valeraldehyde
Valeraldehyde is the common name for the unbranched five-carbon saturated aliphatic aldehyde \(\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_3CHO}\). The systematic IUPAC name for this five-carbon aldehyde is Pentanal. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the systematic nomenclature of Phthaldehyde
Phthaldehyde comprises a benzene ring bearing two adjacent formyl (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)) groups at positions 1 and 2 (\(\mathrm{C_6H_4(CHO)_2}\)). In systematic nomenclature, both aldehyde carbons are treated as substituents on the aromatic ring, giving Benzene-1,2-dicarbaldehyde. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the systematic nomenclature of Mesityl oxide
Mesityl oxide has the structure \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CH\text{-}CO\text{-}CH_3}\). Numbering the five-carbon chain to give the ketone carbonyl the lowest locant yields the carbonyl at position 2, a double bond between carbon-3 and carbon-4, and a methyl branch at carbon-4. Thus, its IUPAC name is 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q03 - Named synthetic reactions and reagents for aldehydes

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Named Reaction)List-II (Reagent and Substrate)
A. Rosenmund reductionI. \(\mathrm{SnCl_2 + HCl}\) followed by \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\) with nitriles
B. Stephen reactionII. \(\mathrm{H_2 / Pd\text{-}BaSO_4}\) with acyl chlorides
C. Étard reactionIII. \(\mathrm{CO, HCl / \text{Anhyd.} AlCl_3}\) with benzene
D. Gatterman-Koch reactionIV. \(\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2 / CS_2}\) followed by \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\) with toluene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Rosenmund reduction
In the Rosenmund reduction, an acyl chloride (acid chloride) is selectively hydrogenated over a poisoned catalyst of palladium supported on barium sulphate (\(\mathrm{Pd\text{-}BaSO_4}\)) to produce the corresponding aldehyde without further reduction to alcohol. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of Stephen reaction
In the Stephen reaction, nitriles are reduced using stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid (\(\mathrm{SnCl_2 + HCl}\)) to give an intermediate iminium salt, which upon subsequent aqueous acid hydrolysis yields an aldehyde. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of Étard reaction
In the Étard reaction, toluene is treated with chromyl chloride (\(\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}\)) in carbon disulfide or carbon tetrachloride to form a brown chromium complex, which on hydrolysis with water yields benzaldehyde. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of Gatterman-Koch reaction
In the Gatterman-Koch reaction, benzene or an alkylbenzene derivative is formulated directly to benzaldehyde upon treatment with a gaseous mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride (\(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\)) or cuprous chloride catalyst. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q04 - Derivatives of aldehydes and ketones with ammonia derivatives

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reagent \(\mathrm{H_2N-Z}\))List-II (Carbonyl Product Class)
A. Hydroxylamine (\(\mathrm{Z = -OH}\))I. Hydrazone
B. Hydrazine (\(\mathrm{Z = -NH_2}\))II. Oxime
C. Semicarbazide (\(\mathrm{Z = -NHCONH_2}\))III. Phenylhydrazone
D. Phenylhydrazine (\(\mathrm{Z = -NHC_6H_5}\))IV. Semicarbazone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the reaction with Hydroxylamine
When aldehydes or ketones react with hydroxylamine (\(\mathrm{NH_2OH}\)), nucleophilic addition followed by elimination of a water molecule yields a condensation product containing the \(>\mathrm{C=N\text{-}OH}\) group, termed an oxime. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the reaction with Hydrazine
When aldehydes or ketones react with hydrazine (\(\mathrm{NH_2NH_2}\)), condensation results in elimination of water to form a product bearing the \(>\mathrm{C=N\text{-}NH_2}\) linkage, known as a hydrazone. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the reaction with Semicarbazide
When aldehydes or ketones condense with semicarbazide (\(\mathrm{NH_2NHCONH_2}\)), only the hydrazine nitrogen (\(-\mathrm{NH_2}\)) acts as the active nucleophile because the amide nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the adjacent carbonyl group. The resulting derivative containing the \(>\mathrm{C=N\text{-}NHCONH_2}\) moiety is named a semicarbazone. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the reaction with Phenylhydrazine
Reaction of aldehydes or ketones with phenylhydrazine (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5NHNH_2}\)) produces crystalline derivatives characterised by the \(>\mathrm{C=N\text{-}NHC_6H_5}\) structure, designated as phenylhydrazones. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q05 - Chemical tests and reagents for distinguishing carbonyl compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reagent / Test)List-II (Characteristic Observation)
A. Tollens' reagentI. Red-brown precipitate with aliphatic aldehydes on heating
B. Fehling's reagentII. Shining silver mirror on the clean inner glass wall
C. 2,4-DinitrophenylhydrazineIII. Yellow precipitate with compounds possessing a methyl ketone group
D. Sodium hypoiodite (\(\mathrm{I_2 / NaOH}\))IV. Yellow, orange, or red crystalline precipitate with carbonyl group

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Tollens' test observation
Tollens' reagent is an ammoniacal silver nitrate solution (\([\mathrm{Ag(NH_3)_2}]^+\)). On gentle warming with aldehydes (both aliphatic and aromatic), the aldehyde is oxidised to carboxylate while silver ions are reduced to metallic silver, depositing as a brilliant shining silver mirror on the clean inner wall of the test tube. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Fehling's test observation
Fehling's reagent consists of Fehling solution A (aqueous \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\)) and Fehling solution B (alkaline sodium potassium tartrate). On heating with aliphatic aldehydes, cupric ions are reduced to cuprous oxide (\(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\)), depositing as a characteristic red-brown precipitate. Aromatic aldehydes fail to respond to this test. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the 2,4-DNP test observation
2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine (Brady's reagent) condenses rapidly with both aldehydes and ketones to produce bright yellow, orange, or red crystalline 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone precipitates. This reaction serves as a universal qualitative test for the presence of the carbonyl functional group. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Sodium hypoiodite test observation
Treatment with iodine and aqueous sodium hydroxide (\(\mathrm{I_2 + NaOH}\), generating sodium hypoiodite \(\mathrm{NaOI}\)) oxidises compounds containing the \(\mathrm{CH_3\text{-}C=O}\) or \(\mathrm{CH_3\text{-}CH(OH)-}\) unit, precipitating triiodomethane (iodoform, \(\mathrm{CHI_3}\)) as a characteristic yellow crystalline solid. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q06 - Substrates and products of condensation and disproportionation reactions

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reactant System)List-II (Major Product Formed)
A. Ethanal treated with dil. \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) and heatedI. Benzyl alcohol and Benzoate ion
B. Benzaldehyde treated with conc. \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) and heatedII. But-2-enal
C. Benzaldehyde + Acetophenone with dil. \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at 293 KIII. 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one
D. Propanone treated with \(\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}\) and heatedIV. 1,3-Diphenylprop-2-en-1-one

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the aldol condensation of Ethanal
Ethanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)) possesses \(\alpha\)-hydrogens. Treatment with dilute sodium hydroxide initiates aldol addition to form 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol). Subsequent heating causes spontaneous dehydration (loss of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) to yield the conjugated \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated aldehyde But-2-enal (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CHO}\)). Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Cannizzaro reaction of Benzaldehyde
Benzaldehyde (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}\)) lacks \(\alpha\)-hydrogens. When heated with concentrated alkali (\(50\%\ \mathrm{NaOH}\)), it undergoes self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation via the Cannizzaro reaction). One molecule is reduced to Benzyl alcohol (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}\)) while the other is oxidised to Benzoate ion (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5COO^-}\)). Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the cross-aldol condensation between Benzaldehyde and Acetophenone
In this cross-aldol system, acetophenone supplies the enolate nucleophile (as it has \(\alpha\)-hydrogens) which attacks the electrophilic formyl carbonyl of benzaldehyde (which lacks \(\alpha\)-hydrogens). Dehydration of the resulting \(\beta\)-hydroxy ketone produces 1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one (commonly known as benzalacetophenone). Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the aldol condensation of Propanone
Propanone (\(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\)) in the presence of barium hydroxide [\(\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}\)] undergoes aldol addition to give diacetone alcohol (4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one). Subsequent heating eliminates a water molecule to generate the conjugated unsaturated ketone 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one (mesityl oxide). Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q07 - Industrial applications of aldehydes ketones and carboxylic acids

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Chemical Substance)List-II (Industrial / Commercial Use)
A. Formalin (40% aqueous HCHO)I. Industrial manufacture of nylon-6,6 polymer
B. Adipic acid (Hexanedioic acid)II. Preservation of biological specimens
C. Ethanoic acid (Acetic acid)III. Preservative used in packaged food products
D. Sodium benzoateIV. Industrial solvent and table vinegar in food industry

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the application of Formalin
A 40% aqueous solution of methanal (formaldehyde) is known commercially as formalin. It crosslinks cellular proteins and is widely utilised for preserving biological and anatomical specimens, as well as in the manufacture of bakelite. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the application of Adipic acid
Adipic acid (hexanedioic acid, \(\mathrm{HOOC(CH_2)_4COOH}\)) is a straight-chain dicarboxylic acid that undergoes polycondensation with hexamethylenediamine to produce the polyamide fiber nylon-6,6. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the application of Ethanoic acid
Ethanoic acid (acetic acid) is produced on a large scale for use as an industrial solvent, in the synthesis of cellulose acetate, and in diluted form (\(5\text{--}8\%\)) as household vinegar in the food processing industry. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the application of Sodium benzoate
Sodium benzoate (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5COONa}\)), the sodium salt of benzoic acid, exhibits potent antimicrobial and antifungal action in acidic media and is widely added as a food preservative in beverages, jams, and pickles. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q08 - Acid strength and pKa values of substituted carboxylic acids

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Carboxylic Acid)List-II (Approximate \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) Value & Rationale)
A. \(\mathrm{CF_3COOH}\)I. \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 1.68\); strongly acidic due to powerful \(-I\) effect of nitro group
B. \(\mathrm{NO_2CH_2COOH}\)II. \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 0.23\); extremely strong acid due to three electronegative fluorine atoms
C. \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\)III. \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 4.76\); weaker acid due to electron-donating \(+I\) effect of methyl group
D. \(\mathrm{HCOOH}\)IV. \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 3.75\); intermediate acid lacking an electron-donating alkyl substituent

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Trifluoroacetic acid
In trifluoroacetic acid (\(\mathrm{CF_3COOH}\)), three intensely electronegative fluorine atoms exert a potent cumulative electron-withdrawing inductive effect (\(-I\)). This heavily disperses the negative charge of the carboxylate anion, stabilising it to an exceptional degree. Consequently, it is an extremely strong organic acid with a very low \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) of approximately 0.23. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of Nitroacetic acid
In nitroacetic acid (\(\mathrm{NO_2CH_2COOH}\)), the strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group (\(-\mathrm{NO_2}\)) exerts a powerful \(-I\) effect across the single methylene carbon. This significantly enhances carboxylate anion stability relative to unsubstituted acetic acid, giving an approximate \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) of 1.68. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of Acetic acid
In acetic acid (\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\)), the methyl group is an electron-releasing substituent through positive inductive effect (\(+I\)). This increases the electron density on the carboxylate group, destabilising the conjugate base and diminishing acidity relative to formic acid, resulting in a higher \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) of 4.76. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 4: Evaluation of Formic acid
In formic acid (\(\mathrm{HCOOH}\)), only a hydrogen atom is attached directly to the carboxyl group. Because hydrogen does not exert an electron-donating inductive effect like an alkyl group, the formate anion is more stable than the acetate anion, conferring an intermediate \(\mathrm{p}K_a\) of 3.75. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with III, and entry D associates with IV.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q09 - Synthetic routes for the preparation of carboxylic acids

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Starting Precursor)List-II (Reagent and Reaction Sequence to Form Acid)
A. Toluene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_3}\))I. Carboxylation using solid \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) followed by hydronium ion workup
B. Grignard reagent (\(\mathrm{RMgX}\))II. Alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) oxidation under heating followed by acid hydrolysis
C. Primary alcohol (\(\mathrm{RCH_2OH}\))III. Stepwise acid or base catalysed hydrolysis via an amide intermediate
D. Nitrile (\(\mathrm{R\text{-}C\equiv N}\))IV. Direct oxidation with Jones reagent (\(\mathrm{CrO_3\text{-}H_2SO_4}\)) in aqueous acetone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the conversion of Toluene to benzoic acid
Primary and secondary alkylbenzenes are vigorously oxidised by heating with alkaline potassium permanganate (\(\mathrm{KMnO_4 / KOH}\)). The entire benzylic aliphatic side chain is cleaved down to potassium benzoate, which upon subsequent acid hydrolysis (\(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)) furnishes benzoic acid. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the conversion of Grignard reagent to carboxylic acid
Grignard reagents (\(\mathrm{RMgX}\)) undergo nucleophilic addition to electrophilic carbon dioxide (solid \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) or dry ice) in anhydrous ether to form a magnesium halocarboxylate salt. Subsequent protonation with aqueous mineral acid (\(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)) yields a carboxylic acid possessing one more carbon than the alkyl halide. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the oxidation of Primary alcohol to carboxylic acid
Primary aliphatic alcohols (\(\mathrm{RCH_2OH}\)) are cleanly oxidised directly to carboxylic acids without isolation of the aldehyde intermediate when treated with Jones reagent (chromium trioxide in dilute aqueous sulphuric acid and acetone, \(\mathrm{CrO_3\text{-}H_2SO_4}\)). Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the hydrolysis of Nitriles to carboxylic acids
Nitriles (\(\mathrm{RCN}\)) contain carbon with a formal oxidation state corresponding to a carboxylic acid derivative. Hydrolysis in the presence of an acid or basic catalyst initially hydrates the triple bond to an intermediate carboxamide (\(\mathrm{RCONH_2}\)), which upon sustained heating with catalyst undergoes complete hydrolysis to produce the carboxylic acid. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_LIST_Q10 - Chemical transformations and reactions of carboxylic acid derivatives

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Chemical Reaction)List-II (Reagent Conditions and Distinguishing Feature)
A. Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reactionI. Decarboxylation of alkali metal salt by electrolysis to yield alkane
B. Kolbe electrolytic reactionII. Halogenation at \(\alpha\)-position using \(\mathrm{X_2 / \text{red P}}\) followed by \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)
C. Phthalic acid with excess \(\mathrm{NH_3}\)III. Formation of acyl chloride with escaping gaseous by-products (\(\mathrm{SO_2, HCl}\))
D. Reaction of carboxylic acid with \(\mathrm{SOCl_2}\)IV. Heating gives diamide; strong heating causes cyclisation to phthalimide

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction
Carboxylic acids possessing at least one \(\alpha\)-hydrogen undergo selective halogenation exclusively at the \(\alpha\)-position when treated with chlorine or bromine in the presence of catalytic amounts of red phosphorus, followed by aqueous workup. This transformation is known as the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction. Hence, entry A correctly corresponds to descriptor II.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Kolbe electrolytic reaction
When an aqueous solution of a sodium or potassium salt of a carboxylic acid is subjected to electrolysis, anodic oxidation and subsequent decarboxylation produces free alkyl radicals that couple to yield an alkane possessing an even number of carbon atoms. This synthetic process is known as Kolbe electrolysis. Hence, entry B correctly corresponds to descriptor I.

Step 3: Evaluation of the reaction of Phthalic acid with ammonia
Treating benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid (phthalic acid) with ammonia initially forms ammonium phthalate. Upon mild heating, two moles of water are eliminated to give phthalamide. Sustained strong heating causes intramolecular condensation with elimination of one mole of ammonia gas to yield the cyclic imide, phthalimide. Hence, entry C correctly corresponds to descriptor IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of the reaction with Thionyl chloride
When a carboxylic acid is treated with thionyl chloride (\(\mathrm{SOCl_2}\)), the hydroxyl moiety is substituted by chlorine to yield an acyl chloride. This method is preferred over phosphorus halides because the co-products sulfur dioxide (\(\mathrm{SO_2}\)) and hydrogen chloride (\(\mathrm{HCl}\)) are both volatile gases that easily escape the reaction vessel, providing the acid chloride in high purity. Hence, entry D correctly corresponds to descriptor III.

Step 5: Final Synthesis and Matching Summary
Synthesizing the individual evaluations yields the correspondence: entry A associates with II, entry B associates with I, entry C associates with IV, and entry D associates with III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
